text: DSH Follow-up Suggestions 是网页端会话提问辅助插件，在最新已完成回复下显示当前模型生成的后续问题。点击建议会填入输入框供用户修改，不会自动发送；也可刷新建议。它只使用当前会话最近的用户消息和助手回复，并按轮次缓存结果。适合想继续追问或快速构思下一条消息的 DSH 用户，需要可用的会话模型服务。

DSH Follow-up Suggestions adds prompts under the latest reply in the DSH web client. It uses the session’s model and recent messages. Clicking a chip fills the composer for editing without sending. Users can refresh suggestions, cached by turn.
想让 DSH 在每条回答下面推荐几个可以继续问的问题。
给我一些和当前对话相关的下一步提问，点了先放进输入框。
DSH 能根据当前会话用的模型生成后续问题吗？
我经常不知道怎么接着问，想要一键填入但不自动发送的建议。
Suggest a few relevant follow-up prompts beneath the latest answer in my DSH chat.
I want clickable next-message ideas that fill the composer but do not send automatically.
DSH Follow-up Suggestions 从会话记录的请求头读取当前 provider 和 model，并用最近的用户消息及助手回复生成建议。
DSH Follow-up Suggestions 只在当前会话最新的已完成回复下显示建议按钮；点击后将文本填入输入框并聚焦，用户可修改后再发送。
DSH Follow-up Suggestions caches prompts by turn for reuse and offers a refresh button to request a new batch.

dsh-followup-suggestions README · Follow-up Suggestions：[](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)

[](LICENSE)

A DSH plugin that renders 1-3 follow-up suggestion chips directly under a session's **last completed reply**. The text is produced by **the model that session has selected**; a click fills the composer and puts your cursor in it, never sending anything. A small refresh icon next to the label asks for one fresh batch.

dsh-followup-suggestions README · Follow-up Suggestions：This repository carries the [`dsh-plugin`](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) topic, which the DeepSeek Harness documentation requires of plugin repositories so they can be discovered; the link above is the inline, clickable form of that requirement.

```
assistant: The Luding Bridge assault happened in May 1935 …
[copy] [branch] …
Suggested ↻
┌──────────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────┐

dsh-followup-suggestions README · What it does：- **Generates** on the Host: it reads the Session's logged request header (`session.requestHeader().config`) for the `provider/model` you picked in `/model` or the composer's model menu, and runs one **one-shot** `ctx.llm.stream()` call for 1-3 short lines.
- **Renders** into ui-chat's `conversation.chat.turnTail` seat on the Client, ordered with `order:1` so the row sits **below** the copy/branch action strip.
- **Only the last reply**: shown only when the Turn record is `status === "closed"` **and** it is the newest entry in `timeline.turnOrder`. Scrollback never requests or shows chips.
- **Click = fill the composer and enter the input state** through ui-conversation's `inputActions.setDraft()`, followed by a focus on the composer's contenteditable with the caret placed at the end of the text — so you can keep typing immediately. It never sends.
- **Refresh = one fresh batch**: the icon after the label asks the Host for this Turn's suggestions again, bypasses both caches on purpose, and replaces the chips on screen and the batch cached for that Turn. A refresh that fails or comes back empty changes nothing, so the chips you are read

dsh-followup-suggestions README · Install：**Option 1 — plugin manager**

```
plugin_manager install_bundle target="github:YubaiLoving/dsh-followup-suggestions"
```

**Option 2 — manual**

The package directory must live under the profile's `node_modules`, with one Loader entry at the end of `cordis.patch.yml` (one row mounts **both** halves):

```
~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-followup-suggestions/
```

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: followup-suggestions
      name: 'dsh-followup-suggestions'
```

dsh-followup-suggestions README · Install：Two notes on that row. First, the package ships its own `cordis.patch.yml` (declared through `dsh.bundle.patch`); when your profile applies bundle patches, that file already inserts the identical row, so do **not** add a second one. Second, the row above is all the Host and Client halves need — a separate **top-level override** row with the same id and no `insert` is only what makes the plugin addressable (and therefore switchable) on the plugin page:

dsh-followup-suggestions README · Install：DSH re-applies the patch layer in place: the **browser half needs a page refresh**, while the **Host half only picks up code changes after a DSH restart** (loaded modules are cached in the process). Changing the entry's `config`, however, **reloads the plugin immediately** (verified: setting `maxItems: 1` made the very next request return one chip). The refresh button is exempt from the restart rule: it also carries a cache-missing synthetic sequence, so pressing it regenerates for real even while the Host is still the older build that ignores `refresh`.

dsh-followup-suggestions README · Install troubleshooting：Three environment-level failures account for almost every "the chips are gone" report. None of them is a plugin bug, and any one of them aborts the whole `pnpm install` — which is why the symptom shows up as a plugin that silently stops appearing rather than as an error in the UI.

dsh-followup-suggestions README · Install troubleshooting：| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ERR_PNPM_FETCH_403` on `GET https://www.npmjs.com/package/<pkg>` | pnpm 11 re-verifies each lockfile entry against its supply-chain policy and fetches the npm **website** page for the package; that request can be refused with 403 while `registry.npmjs.org` still answers 200 — a proxy or bot-protection issue, not a problem with the package | rerun the install with the re-verification skipped: `pnpm install --trust-lockfile` (verified: turns a hard failure into a successful install in seconds) |
| `ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED` | another dependency in the same profile comes from git and wants to run build scripts, but is not allowlisted | add that package to `allowBuilds` in the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, using the exact key the message prints (`'<name>@<resolved-url>': true`) |
| You edited this plugin's source, but the running DSH still behaves the old way | a `file:` dependency is **copied** into the profile, not symlinked, so the install froze the source as it was at install time | rerun the install inside the profile directory after every source edit; a Host-h

dsh-followup-suggestions README · Install troubleshooting：An aborted install does not tear down what already worked — but the package being added or relinked never lands, so a plugin can disappear between two restarts. Check what is really installed before debugging anything else:

```

dsh-followup-suggestions README · Windows path shown; adapt to your OS：node -p "require('C:/Users/<you>/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-followup-suggestions/package.json').version"
```

Then confirm the roster still carries the plugin (in `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml`, the id must be present both in the `insert` list and as a top-level row).

dsh-followup-suggestions README · Configuration (optional)：Add a `config` block to the entry in `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: followup-suggestions
  name: 'dsh-followup-suggestions'
  config:
    maxItems: 3           # 1-3; anything higher is clamped to 3

Every field may be omitted. `config` changes take effect immediately (the plugin reloads; no restart).

dsh-followup-suggestions README · How it works：| Concern | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Model choice | Routing comes entirely from the Session's own request header — the plugin has **no** model setting of its own, so switching models with `/model` switches the suggestions too |
| Context | `session.deriveMessages()`: the last user text plus the last assistant text, each trimmed to 1200 characters of tail |
| Call | `ctx.llm.stream({ provider, model, maxTokens, reasoningEffort, sessionId, messages, signal })` with an `AbortSignal.timeout` guard; `BlockAssembler` collects the stream |
| Transport | Host registers `POST /api/dsh-followup-suggest` through `ctx.connection.fetch.register()`; the Client uses a same-origin `fetch` |
| Placement | `ctx.slots.inject("conversation.chat.turnTail", …)`. The seat's outlet wrapper is `display:contents`, so this row is a sibling of the action strip and `order:1` puts it below (if that container ever stops being a flex column the declaration is ignored and the row falls back above the strip) |
| Effort | The lowest effort is requested with a `maxTokens` cap. A route that does not know the effort answers `UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT`; the call is then
dsh-followup-suggestions README · Performance：There are two costs: the **model call** (the only significant one) and **rendering**. Measured locally, on real sessions with a real model:

dsh-followup-suggestions README · Performance：| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repeated request for one Turn (Host cache hit) | ~1.5–2.4 s, unstable text | **~5 ms**, identical text |
| Reload / switch away and back | One model call each time | **0 calls** (painted with the reply) |
| First load (a call is unavoidable) | ~2 s of nothing, then a pop-in | Three **placeholder pills** immediately, replaced when the answer lands |
| Two tabs asking at the same instant | Two model calls | **One** (shared in-flight promise) |

dsh-followup-suggestions README · Performance：On the lowest reasoning effort: an interleaved A/B (2×5 calls per arm against the same live Host, toggling the entry's `config`) found **no measurable latency difference** — median 1413 ms inherited vs 1495 ms `off`, inside the noise, because first-token time from the provider dominates. It is kept for reliability: the answer is very short, so a route that inherits a high effort spends the output budget thinking and can truncate below three lines when `maxTokens` is small (4 of 10 calls in the inherited arm returned fewer than three chips; the `off` arm returned three 10 times out of 10). Per-call latency is unchanged; what this plugin optimizes is **repeated work** and **perceived latency**.

dsh-followup-suggestions README · Known limitations：- **Only the last reply of the session you are viewing**: intentional (fewer calls, no noise), not precomputed per session.
- **Two DOM/seat contracts**: a Turn record carrying `status`/`turn`, and `useChat().timeline.turnOrder`. If ui-chat changes either, `lib/client.js` needs the matching update.
- **Depends on ui-conversation's `inputActions` and composer DOM**: without that seat the chips still render but clicking does nothing; if `data-conversation-content`/`data-conversation-session`/`data-composer-input` are renamed, a click still fills the draft but no longer moves the keyboard.
- **Cached chips live 7 days by default**: one Turn's suggestions stay stable that long, and the refresh icon is the way to ask for a new batch. Clearing `dsh.followupSuggestions.v1` from `localStorage` does the same thing by hand.
- **A refresh costs one model call**: by design — it is the only action that bypasses both caches.
- **The Host cache is process memory**: nothing is written to disk and it empties on restart.
- **Host-side code changes need a restart**: loaded modules are cached in the process (entry `config` changes are the exception —
